findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: This base very likely lacks the systems schema, so the job as planned would stop at step 1 and land nothing.
findings.evidence: Read and grep of this snapshot: crates/athena-data/src/config.rs has only the per-capability repo_url/repo_ref (lines 413-416). athena.toml has one [capabilities.study] section with repo_url/repo_ref at lines 105-106 and no systems table. pin_repo (run/pin.rs:33-43) reads that single section. HISTORY.txt has no commit adding a systems schema; a grep for 'systems' and 'hermes' found only an unrelated Hermes/Hestia design commit. The request says Athena must be reinstalled from a main that holds the schema, but the job's base is this tree. Fix: Keep the stop-and-report rule. Have Athena or the owner confirm that the job's base commit holds the schema before dispatch, for example by rebasing the job onto a main that has it, so a producer run is not spent only to stop at step 1.

findings.summary: In case B the reader's view comes from a substring match on system ids. This is a heuristic that can misfire on paths and on ids that are prefixes of other ids.
findings.evidence: study_pin already uses request.contains(study) (pin.rs:117). The plan reuses that selector style and corrects false positives with a full-tree re-read, at the cost of one extra reader run. The plan prefers a dedicated selector (case A) when one exists, and asks the user about the cost. Fix: No change needed for this round. In the final report, recommend that the systems schema gain an explicit selector so case B can be removed later.
findings.location: Decision 4, case B (substring selector for the reader view)

findings.summary: Athena's own finding: scope_guard.rs is outside the reading's deliverables. The plan's conditional handling is sound and is not repeated here.
findings.evidence: scope_guard.rs:1054-1058 drops every line starting with repo_url or repo_ref from the repository's athena.toml. The new table could then be left with no keys. Grep confirmed this. Fix: Keep the edit conditional on the step 1(c) result, and name the file in the final report if it is edited.

summary: I checked the round-5 plan against the code with Read and Grep; I ran no commands. The places the plan names exist where it says: Snapshot::create callers at planning.rs:138/292, producer.rs:146, verification.rs:455 and checks.rs:955; verifier_snapshot calls at mod.rs:1937, verification.rs:313/341 and checks.rs:663; the Checked destructure at verification.rs:40-50, before candidate_view at :58; the 'not a check' entry pattern at :100-112; and study_pin's exact-URL match at pin.rs:99. Hiding is keyed on the job's recorded pin URL. That is correct because firstmate's pin.json repository_url (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git) equals its configured repo_url, while its directory name (firstmate-work-handling) is not the system id. The gate stays on the full tree, which is right: real tests embed or read studies/firstmate-work-handling. The producer and verifier agents are told in code, outside the always-loaded prompt sets, so token budgets do not change. Hidden directories never enter the snapshot repository. So change_list cannot report them as deleted, and build_candidate keeps their base blobs. Criterion 3's fixture covers this with an intervention commit, a stray write under the hidden directory and a gate check, and the plan includes the commit-shape table. Each demonstration names a real seam (Athena::ask/go, FakeAgentDriver with a Tweak, CountingPinner, Snapshot::create_hiding) and would fail without the behavior. The dependents list covers the readers of the changed functions and of the firstmate study. The main practical risk is that this snapshot's base lacks the systems schema, so step 1 would stop the job; the plan handles that correctly. No blocker or major finding remains.
